blocks.heading_context: ## The Big Picture: Revolution in Military Affairs Timeline
blocks.text:
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|              REVOLUTION IN MILITARY AFFAIRS (RMA) CYCLE          |
|                                                                  |
|  Technology       Dominant System     Vulnerability Created      |
|  Disruption       Enabled             Counter Doctrine           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  Bronze Age       Chariot + composite  Flanks / rough terrain    |
|  metallurgy       bow (shock + range)  -> Phalanx / skirmish     |
|                                                                  |
|  Iron Age         Heavy infantry       Concentrated mass         |
|  weapons          (cheaper armor)      -> Oblique / envelopment  |
|                                                                  |
|  Stirrup          Armored cavalry      Unsupported flanks        |
|  (~700 AD)        (shock charge)       -> Crossbow / pike square |
|                                                                  |
|  Gunpowder        Cannon               High vertical stone walls |
|  (~1300 AD)       (siege artillery)    -> Trace italienne        |
|                                                                  |
|  Rifled musket    Line infantry        Dense formations exposed  |
|  + Minie ball     firepower            -> Entrenchment / cover   |
|  (~1850)                                                         |
|                                                                  |
|  Machine gun +    Defended position    Offensive assault stalled |
|  barbed wire      (firepower density)  -> Tank / infiltration    |
|  (~1900)                                                         |
|                                                                  |
|  Tank + radio     Blitzkrieg combined  Static linear defense     |
|  (~1939)          arms                 -> Anti-tank depth        |
|                                                                  |
|  Precision        Standoff strike      Massed armor / formations |
|  munitions +      (GPS/laser)          -> A2/AD / dispersion     |
|  stealth (~1991)                                                 |
|                                                                  |
|  Cyber + AI       Network-centric C2   All connected systems     |
|  (~2010+)         (information edge)   targetable -> resilience  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

Pattern: new weapon -> dominant tactic -> new vulnerability ->
counter-doctrine -> next RMA. Armies that mastered last war's
doctrine and did not adapt get destroyed.

+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    CLAUSEWITZ'S TRINITY                     |
|                                                             |
|                 [ THE STATE ]                               |
|                 Government / Reason / Policy aims           |
|                        /              \                     |
|                       /                \                    |
|        [ THE PEOPLE ]              [ THE MILITARY ]         |
|        Passion / Hatred             Chance / Skill /        |
|        Primordial violence          Friction / Fog of war   |
|                                                             |
|  All three must remain in tension. Break any leg:           |
|  - State loses popular support -> political collapse        |
|  - Military operates without policy aims -> strategic       |
|    drift (MacArthur, Korea 1950-51)                         |
|  - Passion without state control -> genocide / atrocity     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+

Core thesis: "War is the continuation of politics by other means."
Not a metaphor — a precise claim that war is always a political
instrument. A war that loses connection to achievable political
objectives becomes purposeless violence.

+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    THREE LEVELS OF WAR                         |
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                 |
|  STRATEGIC        What do we want to ACHIEVE politically?      |
|  (NSC, head of    | "Defeat Germany, restore European balance" |
|   state, CJCS)   | Time horizon: months to years              |
|                   | Currency: national power, alliances,       |
|                   |   political will, economic resources       |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|                                |                                |
|                                v                                |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|  OPERATIONAL      HOW do we orchestrate military force to      |
|  (theater         | achieve strategic goals?                   |
|   commanders,     | "Encircle Army Group South, cut supply     |
|   army groups)    |  lines, force surrender at Stalingrad"    |
|                   | Time horizon: weeks to months              |
|                   | Currency: logistics, operational maneuver, |
|                   |   campaign design, lines of operation      |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|                                |                                |
|                                v                                |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|  TACTICAL         HOW do we win individual engagements?        |
|  (battalion and   | "Take that ridge before nightfall"         |
|   below)          | Time horizon: hours to days                |
|                   | Currency: firepower, maneuver, terrain,    |
|                   |   unit cohesion, initiative                |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|

KEY INSIGHT: You can win every tactical engagement and still lose
the war. The US military won essentially every significant tactical
engagement in Vietnam. It lost strategically because the political
objective (a stable independent South Vietnam) required more
sustained will than the domestic political environment could sustain.

Tactical excellence must serve operational design, which must serve
strategic purpose. When any level pursues its own logic independently
of the others, strategic failure follows.

+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     DOCTRINE CYCLE                            |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                               |
|   1. NEW TECHNOLOGY EMERGES                                   |
|      (rifled musket, tank, JDAM, social media)               |
|      Average lead time before military adoption: 5-20 years  |
|              |                                                |
|              v                                                |
|   2. DOCTRINE DEVELOPMENT                                     |
|      Military theorists + combat practitioners work out      |
|      how to use the new tool effectively. This is the        |
|      hard intellectual work — Mitchell on airpower, Guderian |
|      on tanks, Cebrowski on network-centric warfare.         |
|      Early adopters with correct doctrine gain decisive      |
|      advantage. Wrong doctrine + right technology = loss.    |
|              |                                                |
|              v                                                |
|   3. WIDESPREAD ADOPTION + CODIFICATION                       |
|      Doctrine written into field manuals, taught at war      |
|      colleges, exercised at NTC/JRTC. Advantage narrows      |
|      as adversaries copy or develop counters.                |
|              |                                                |
|              v                                                |
|   4. COUNTER-DOCTRINE EMERGES                                 |
|      Tech counter: APC vs machine gun, anti-tank missile     |
|        vs tank, shoulder-launched SAM vs close air support.  |
|      Doctrinal counter: different employment concept that    |
|        negates the dominant tactic without matching tech.    |
|        (asymmetric approaches, IED campaigns, cyber)         |
|              |                                                |
|              v                                                |
|   5. NEXT RMA BEGINS OR DOCTRINE STAGNATES                   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+

Doctrine lag examples:
  France 1940: Had 4,000 tanks (more than Germany). Wrong doctrine —
    dispersed as infantry support vs massed, independent armored
    operational maneuver. Tech parity; doctrinal defeat.

  Israel 1973 (Yom Kippur): Overconfident after 1967. Sinai had good
    tank terrain but Egyptian infantry now had Sagger ATGMs in density
    that made tank charges suicidal without infantry support.
    Forgot the combined arms lesson. ~800 Israeli tanks lost.

  US in Afghanistan: Gulf War doctrine (air-ground combined arms,
    precision strike) highly effective against conventional forces.
    Mismatched against distributed insurgency — doctrinal lag.

+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|              RECURRING STRATEGIC FAILURE PATTERNS             |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                               |
|  MIRROR IMAGING          Assuming enemy will fight your way.  |
|  (cognitive bias)         Germany assumed France 1940 would   |
|                           hold reserves behind the Maginot    |
|                           Line as they would. France assumed  |
|                           Ardennes impassable as they did.    |
|                                                               |
|  POLITICAL OVERRIDE      Operational logic overridden for     |
|  OF OPERATIONS            domestic political reasons.         |
|                           Hitler's no-retreat orders (1942)   |
|                           vs operational flexibility need.    |
|                           LBJ's bombing halt negotiations     |
|                           telegraphed US will limits.         |
|                                                               |
|  METRIC SUBSTITUTION     Measuring what you can count, not    |
|  (McNamara pathology)     what matters. Vietnam body count    |
|                           optimized for enemy body count ->   |
|                           inflated numbers, perverse          |
|                           incentives, no strategic meaning.   |
|                                                               |
|  ENDS-MEANS MISMATCH     Strategic objectives requiring more  |
|                           force than politically sustainable. |
|                           US COIN 2003-2021: nation-building  |
|                           required ~50yr commitment, not 20.  |
|                                                               |
|  COALITION FRICTION      Allies with divergent war aims.     |
|                           WWI: France wanted Alsace-Lorraine, |
|                           Britain wanted maritime security,   |
|                           Russia wanted Bosphorus. Hard to    |
|                           coordinate, easy to defect.         |
|                                                               |
|  MOBILIZATION LOCK       Rail/industrial mobilization creates |
|  (July 1914 problem)      momentum impossible to stop. Once  |
|                           ordered, cannot un-mobilize without |
|                           strategic disadvantage. Forces      |
|                           decision before diplomacy can work. |
|                                                               |
|  FAULTY COG ANALYSIS     Attacking the wrong center of       |
|                           gravity. Bombing German cities      |
|                           (civilian morale) vs oil/transport  |
|                           (operational capability). Morale    |
|                           hardened; oil campaign worked.      |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  MILITARY-HISTORY MODULE MAP                     |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  00-OVERVIEW          This file — RMA framework, Clausewitz,    |
|                        levels of war, doctrine cycle             |
|                                                                  |
|  01-ANCIENT           Phalanx, Alexander, Roman legion,         |
|                        logistics, trireme, Cannae                |
|                                                                  |
|  02-MEDIEVAL          Feudal system, castle evolution,          |
|                        siege warfare, Mongols, infantry rise     |
|                                                                  |
|  03-GUNPOWDER         Cannon vs castle, trace italienne,        |
|                        musket drill revolution, naval broadside  |
|                                                                  |
|  04-NAPOLEONIC        Corps system, operational level,          |
|                        Gribeauval artillery, Russia 1812         |
|                                                                  |
|  05-INDUSTRIAL        Rifled weapons, railways, ironclads,      |
|                        Civil War, machine gun + wire deadlock    |
|                                                                  |
|  06-WORLD-WAR-I       Stalemate mechanics, attrition logic,    |
|                        Somme, tank/gas/aircraft emergence        |
|                                                                  |
|  07-WORLD-WAR-II      Blitzkrieg, carrier aviation,            |
|                        strategic bombing, logistics, nuclear     |
|                                                                  |
|  08-COLD-WAR-NUCLEAR  Deterrence theory, limited war,          |
|                        Vietnam COIN, AirLand Battle              |
|                                                                  |
|  09-MODERN-PRECISION  Gulf War RMA, network-centric,           |
|                        COIN rise and fall, drones, A2/AD        |
|                                                                  |
|  10-CYBER-INFORMATION Cyberwar domain, Stuxnet, hybrid war,   |
|                        deterrence problems, AI weapons           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
